Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Depressive symptoms decreased significantly after six months of vitamin D supplementation in women with type 2 diabetes.
Sentence: "There was a significant decrease in depression (CES-D and PHQ-9, p < 0.001) and anxiety (state and trait, p < 0.001)."
Measured as: depression (CES-D and PHQ-9)
Population: Fifty women with type 2 diabetes and significant depressive symptomology
Intervention: Ergocalciferol 50,000 IU weekly for six months
Comparator: None (single-arm)
Design: case series
Sample size: 50
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Responses

### Response A
```json
{
 "rationale": "Both single-arm studies report improved depression after vitamin D, but Study B's 15D depression dimension is a score where higher means better, so the 'harm' label comes from the score's direction and the two do not truly conflict.",
 "verdict": "apparent",
 "reason": "outcome_measure",
 "also_differs": [
  "population",
  "intervention"
 ],
 "detail": "15D depression dimension is a quality-of-life item where an increase means improvement, versus CES-D/PHQ-9 where a decrease means improvement; both findings show improvement"
}
```

### Response B
```json
{
 "rationale": "Both single-arm studies report improved depression after vitamin D, so the results do not truly conflict; the 'harm' label reflects a higher 15D score that actually means improvement, while Study A used full depression scales and Study B a single 15D dimension.",
 "verdict": "apparent",
 "reason": "outcome_measure",
 "also_differs": [
  "population",
  "intervention"
 ],
 "detail": "15D depression dimension score (higher = better) vs CES-D/PHQ-9 (lower = better); same direction of improvement"
}
```

### Response C
```json
{
 "rationale": "Both single-arm case series report improved depression after vitamin D, but Study B's 15D depression dimension (a single item of a wider quality-of-life instrument) is not the same construct as Study A's full depression scales; the 'harm' label reflects score direction, not worsening.",
 "verdict": "apparent",
 "reason": "outcome_measure",
 "also_differs": [
  "population",
  "intervention"
 ],
 "detail": "15D depression dimension (one item of a QoL instrument) vs CES-D/PHQ-9 full depression scales; both improved, so no real conflict"
}
```
